answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to slashable bonded collateral: when k identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, pairwise evidence triggers penalties scaling as O(k^2), not merely per-node fines. A swarm concentrates risk; upon detection, capital loss carries an exponential multiplier, with confiscation and asymmetric depreciation magnifying the cost. The sable ledge offers no safe bridge: splitting keys does not erase correlated liability.
